intent: Show that uninsured Americans are most likely to skip medication because of cost, while even insured Americans rank second and above every other compared country.

requirements.question: Which group is most likely to skip medication because of cost?

scope.measure: share skipping prescriptions or doses because of cost

requirements.question: How does the insured U.S. rate compare with the other countries?

scope.measure: share skipping prescriptions or doses because of cost

units.claim: Uninsured Americans have the highest rate at about 33.5%, exceeding insured Americans at about 20.1% and every comparison country at 10.1% or less.
accept: the uninsured U.S. bar is the tallest
uninsured Americans rank first at about 33.5%
the uninsured rate is higher than both insured Americans and every comparison country
reject: insured Americans are described as higher than uninsured Americans
the comparison is presented without the cost-related condition
units.evidence: Eight bars share a percentage scale; the Uninsured United States bar is visibly the tallest.

units.claim: Insured Americans rank second at about 20.1%, still above Canada's highest comparison-country rate of about 10.1%.
accept: the insured U.S. bar is second only to the uninsured U.S. bar
insured Americans have a higher rate than every non-U.S. country
reject: insured Americans are below any comparison country
insured Americans are described as the highest group
Canada or another comparison country is omitted
the 20.1% value is assigned to the uninsured group
units.evidence: The insured U.S. bar is the second-tallest and remains about twice as high as Canada's comparison bar.

optional_valid: The chart concerns cost-related skipping of prescriptions or doses, not all medication nonadherence.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all data rows because the table has no role column
